# AdaptiqAI for OpenCode and Kilo

Your AdaptiqAI workspace in [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) (1.x from 1.18.29,
and 2.x) and in [Kilo](https://kilo.ai): its models, conversations that
AdaptiqAI remembers, and your saved knowledge, in one plugin.

## Install

Add the plugin to the harness's config:

| Harness | Config | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 1.x | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `"plugin": ["@adaptiqai/opencode"]` |
| OpenCode 2.x | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `"plugins": ["@adaptiqai/opencode"]` |
| Kilo | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json` | `"plugin": ["@adaptiqai/opencode"]` |

Then sign in: run `opencode auth login` (or `kilo auth login`, or `/connect`
in the app) and choose **AdaptiqAI**:

- **Sign in with your browser** opens the AdaptiqAI approval page. You sign in
  (or create an account) and approve, and the harness picks it up by itself.
- **AdaptiqAI API key** takes a key from the AdaptiqAI console.
  `ADAPTIQAI_API_KEY` in the environment works too.

Choose a model from the **AdaptiqAI** provider (`adaptiqai/<model>`). The list
is the models in your workspace, each with its own output limit and
thinking levels (OpenCode's variants).

Set up from the AdaptiqAI console's **Connect to app** instead, the harness
gets this plugin by itself, from the configuration that sign-in gives it, and
the plugin takes that sign-in's key. The harness then runs on the console's
own AdaptiqAI provider (`adaptiq/<model>`), and the plugin adds its tools and
`/adaptiq` beside it, but no second provider.

## What it does

- **A conversation is one AdaptiqAI session.** Every turn carries the
  harness's session id as `x-adaptiq-session-id`. AdaptiqAI keeps the
  conversation's memory, and the collections and conversations you attach to
  it in the console reach the model.
- **The harness's own session headers are replaced.** OpenCode and Kilo put
  session headers of their own on every request, title calls too. OpenCode 2
  even puts the root conversation's id in a subagent's `X-Session-Id`. A turn
  goes out with only the plugin's header, a helper call with none.
- **Helper calls leave nothing.** Titles, compaction and summaries run once,
  marked ephemeral, and never become a conversation. So do Kilo's commit
  messages and branch names, and any request the plugin cannot tell is a turn.
- **The harness never compacts an AdaptiqAI conversation by itself.**
  AdaptiqAI holds the conversation whole. The harness's own compaction would
  rewrite that history and make the engine compile the conversation again.
  - The plugin leaves its models' context window unknown, which all three
    harnesses read as "never compact automatically". Every other model keeps
    the harness's compaction.
  - Compacting on purpose (`/compact`) still works, once and ephemeral, but
    an unknown window sizes it less well. OpenCode 1.x and Kilo keep no
    recent messages word for word beside the summary, and Kilo 7.8.15 sums
    up one message per request. OpenCode 2 sums up only as much as fits a
    200k window, and its model list shows the window as 0.
  - A request the gateway refuses as too large (HTTP 413) still makes the
    harness compact.
- **A subagent names the conversation that started it**
  (`X-Adaptiq-Parent-Session-Id`, role `helper`), so the console folds it
  under that conversation.
- **Tools for the agent:**
  - `adaptiq_knowledge`: what this conversation uses; find words, ids or names
    in the text of its collections, with the exact lines as document:line;
    search the library by name, use or stop a collection.
  - `adaptiq_memory`: how full the memory is; the saved collections; keep a
    conversation private.
  - `adaptiq_create_knowledge`: save material as a collection, only when you
    ask.

  In OpenCode 2 they are on the model's own tool list, not behind Code Mode.
- **A turn is told which ready collections its conversation reads**, so the
  agent looks things up there with find. OpenCode 1.x and Kilo save the note
  with your message, as a part you don't see, once and again when the
  collections change; OpenCode 2 keeps nothing a plugin adds, so each request
  carries it in its system prompt. Conversations on the console's own
  provider (Connect to app) get it too.
- **`/adaptiq`** asks the agent where this conversation's memory and
  knowledge stand. OpenCode and Kilo give a plugin's command no way to answer
  by itself, so it is a turn of the model and costs like one. That turn reads
  the conversation and saves nothing: the question and its answer stay out of
  the conversation's memory. Only what you type after `/adaptiq` counts as
  your own words.

Signing out in the harness (`opencode auth logout`, or removing the
credential in OpenCode 2) signs the plugin out too, and the plugin removes
its own copy of the sign-in, refresh token and all:

- OpenCode 2 tells the plugin at once.
- `opencode auth logout` and `kilo auth logout` change only the harness's
  own file. The plugin removes its copy at the next request, or within five
  minutes while the harness runs, or when the harness next starts.

The copy is removed from this computer, not revoked at AdaptiqAI: to
disconnect this computer altogether, use Connected apps in the AdaptiqAI
console.

OpenCode 1.x and 2.x keep separate AdaptiqAI sign-ins, and so does the
plugin: signing out of one leaves the other signed in.

## How it fits each harness

| | OpenCode 1.x and Kilo (`server()`) | OpenCode 2.x (`setup()`) |
|---|---|---|
| Provider and models | added to the config by the `config` hook | `provider.transform`, reloaded when the list changes |
| Sign-in | `auth` methods; the plugin's own fetch signs each request | integration methods; OAuth `refresh` renews OpenCode's copy |
| Turn or helper call | `chat.headers` marks it by agent (and Kilo's session ids) | `model.request` by request kind |
| Session headers | replaced in the plugin's fetch | replaced in `model.request` |
| Memory field | added in the plugin's fetch | added in `http.request` |
| No automatic compaction | window left unknown (`limit.context: 0`) | the same |
| Tools | zod arguments, rebuilt from the core's JSON Schema | the core's JSON Schema, `codemode: false` |

A provider that only the config knows never gets a plugin's model list in
OpenCode 1.x or Kilo, so the models go into the config. The config is read
once as the harness starts (and again when its connect dialog reloads after a
sign-in), so the plugin starts with the models it last listed.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `ADAPTIQAI_API_KEY` | none: the harness's own sign-in |
| `ADAPTIQAI_API_BASE` | `https://api.adaptiqai.com` |
| `ADAPTIQAI_CONSOLE_URL` | `https://memory.adaptiqai.com/memory` |

The browser sign-in, the plugin's state and the last model list are kept in
`adaptiqai/` in the harness's data folder (`~/.local/share/opencode` or
`~/.local/share/kilo`, or under `XDG_DATA_HOME`), readable by you alone.
OpenCode 2 shares OpenCode 1.x's data folder, so its copy is in
`adaptiqai-2/` there.

## Development

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @adaptiqai/opencode run build
pnpm --filter @adaptiqai/opencode run test
```

To try it, put the package folder's absolute path in the config's `plugin`
(or, for OpenCode 2, `plugins`) list.
